data.narrative:
eGenesis is a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Luhan Yang and George Church, having raised $250M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 public-market peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector, with particular weight on 3 same-stage private comparables.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $250M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $425M. Peer-median anchoring draws on three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Colossal Biosciences at $10.3B, Chai Discovery at $3.8B, and New Limit at $3.1B—producing a median implied valuation of $3.8B. The peer range spans $3.1B to $10.3B, reflecting material dispersion across the cohort. Public-comp P/S anchoring is not applicable due to absence of disclosed revenue for the private target.

Triangulation of the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $361M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The wide band reflects tension between the stage-progression floor and peer-median positioning. Key uncertainties include heterogeneity within the peer set—particularly the $10.3B outlier—and the lack of revenue visibility to validate relative multiples. The median estimate of $2.1B provides a conservative anchor relative to peer medians but remains sensitive to technology validation and clinical de-risking milestones.
